issues.legal_issue: A contract that makes repayment of the earnest money and fixed compensation the exclusive consequence of either party declining to complete a sale does not support an order for specific performance.
material_facts: The parties entered into an agreement for the sale of agricultural land, which required a sale deed to be executed by a stated date.

The agreement provided that if either the seller declined to sell or the purchaser declined to buy, the earnest money would be returned with an additional fixed sum, and no sale deed would be executed.
The purchaser’s successor sued for specific performance and, alternatively, repayment of the earnest money and the additional sum.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser’s successors were not entitled to specific performance because the agreement made repayment of the earnest money and the additional sum the only consequence of either party declining to complete the sale.
issues.legal_principle: The parties’ relationship is governed by the terms of their agreement. Where the agreement provides that either party may decline to complete the sale and specifies repayment and fixed compensation as the consequence, it creates no obligation to complete the sale that can be enforced by specific performance. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser or the purchaser’s successor brought a suit seeking to compel completion of a sale.
predicates.agreement_permits_either_party_to_declin: The parties’ agreement provided that either the seller or the purchaser could decline to complete the sale.
predicates.contract_limits_consequence_to_repayment: The agreement specified repayment of the earnest money and fixed compensation as the consequence of declining to complete the sale, and stated that no sale deed would then be executed.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns an agreement that permits either party to decline completion and limits the consequence to repayment and fixed compensation, specific performance is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A fixed sum awarded as compensation for failure to complete a contract may be ordered to carry interest from the date of the trial court’s decree.
material_facts: The trial court ordered repayment of the earnest money with interest from the filing of the suit and awarded an additional fixed sum as damages.
On appeal, the Supreme Court affirmed the trial court’s decree but modified it to provide that the damages would also carry interest from the date of the trial court’s decree.
issues.conclusion: The damages award was to carry interest from the date of the trial court’s decree, in addition to interest on the repayment from the filing of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court modified the monetary decree to award interest on the fixed damages from the date of the trial court’s decree. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this modification.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_contract_decree: A civil appeal concerned a decree in a suit arising from a contract.
predicates.trial_court_awarded_fixed_compensation: The trial court awarded a fixed sum as compensation.
predicates.compensation_arose_from_failure_to_compl: The fixed compensation arose from the parties’ failure to complete the contractual transaction.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal from a contract decree, when the trial court awarded fixed compensation for failure to complete the contract, interest is awarded on that compensation from the date of the decree.
